sections.h2: Where in Morehead do I handle a Rowan County tax bill?
sections.html:
The PVA and the sheriff both operate from the Rowan County Courthouse at 600 West Main Street, open weekdays from 8 AM to 4 PM. The PVA, at (606) 784-5512, assesses all taxable real and personal property, tracks changes of ownership, keeps parcel maps and processes exemptions. The sheriff, at (606) 784-5446, mails and collects the bills.

The county's property tax page says the sheriff takes cash, checks and money orders in person, and accepts cards through an outside vendor that charges 2.49 percent on amounts above $60 and a flat $1.50 below that. Online payment is offered too, with the bill in hand.

When a bill goes delinquent, the County Clerk and the County Attorney take over, and the county's delinquent taxes page describes how those offices work with the sheriff.

sections.h2: What is Rowan County's own payment calendar?
sections.html:
The county lists a discount window that ends on November 30, later than the plain statewide cutoff, and says bills are first handed out at the start of November.

Rowan County, KY: stages for a sheriff's property tax bill, per the county
StageWhat applies
Before November 302 percent discount
By December 31Face amount of the bill
January 1 to January 315 percent penalty
February 1 to April 1521 percent total penalty
After April 15Delinquent, handed to the County Clerk

KRS 134.015 lets the Department of Revenue shift the calendar when mailing runs late, which explains why one year's dates can differ from the standard November 1 cutoff. The tax is the owner's personal debt from January 1, so a seller closing in spring should plan to settle the year's bill.

sections.h2: What would a median Rowan County house owe the state?
sections.html:
The 2025 state rate is 10.6 cents on each hundred dollars of assessment. QuickFacts lists the typical Rowan County home at $161,800, which puts the state's share near $171.51. The county, the school district and other districts add their own rates, and the sheriff can quote the combined figure for an address.

Owners from age 65 and totally disabled owners deduct $49,100 for 2025 and 2026. On the typical home that leaves $112,700 taxable and a state share near $119.46. The PVA at the courthouse takes the application and asks for proof of age such as a license or passport.

Only 61.5 percent of Rowan County homes are occupied by owners, so many parcels are rentals. A landlord who sells should expect the buyer to ask who covers the year's bill.

sections.h2: How does Rowan County pursue delinquent taxes?
sections.html:
Once April 15 passes, the bill sits with the County Clerk, and the county attorney follows a published timetable. Two letters go out on fixed dates, and the sale normally lands in the second week of August.

  • May 15: the County Attorney mails a 30-day notice.
  • June 15: a 60-day notice follows for bills still open.
  • Second week of August: the usual sale, where outside investors may buy a bill and add fees.
  • Each month: the delinquent amount climbs by 1 percent until it is paid.

The owner of record can sign a delinquent tax contract with the County Attorney's office up to three days before the sale. The county requires 10 percent of the bill that day and spreads the rest over monthly payments. A contract signed ahead of the clerk's sale keeps investors from buying the bill.

The County Attorney also presses the county's tax claim in foreclosure cases, where it holds priority.

sections.h2: How can a Rowan County owner contest a valuation?
sections.html:
A conference with the PVA or a deputy is the required first step. The roll stays open for inspection for thirteen days from May's first Monday, and the PVA must advertise the dates in the county's largest newspaper along with appeal instructions. At the conference the PVA explains how your figure was built and keeps a written record.

  • Lodge the appeal at the clerk's office on the workday after the inspection period closes.
  • Prepare evidence: descriptions of land and buildings, insurance policies, construction costs, listings or sales. The board must reject a case with none.
  • Expect a hearing some 25 to 35 days later before a panel of local owners.
  • A paid agent has to belong to a statutory group such as attorneys, CPAs or licensed appraisers.

If bills print before a ruling, your claimed value is used first, and a supplemental bill follows when the board sets a higher number.

sections.h2: Does selling a Rowan County house clear back taxes?
sections.html:
It does not. A lien under KRS 134.420 arises once taxes turn delinquent and lasts eleven years whoever holds title. A title search at the County Clerk will reveal it, and it normally has to be cleared at closing.

A Department of Revenue example shows how fast debt grows after April 15. A $1,000 bill becomes $1,254.00 on transfer, about $1,387.79 inside five business days and $1,611.30 after the county attorney's first notice, before another month of interest. Paying the sheriff on time avoids that.

An owner who is behind has several routes before the August sale: pay the sheriff, pay the clerk, or sign a contract with the County Attorney. A direct cash sale is another option when repairs or inherited debts stand in the way, with the amount owed paid from the proceeds.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Rowan County itself?
sections.html:
Rowan County was carved out in 1856 from parts of Fleming and Morgan counties and lies in the Eastern Kentucky Coalfield, with about 280 square miles of land. Morehead is the seat and Lakeview Heights the other city. Morehead was incorporated in 1869, holds close to 7,000 people, and hosts Morehead State University, Cave Run Lake, Rowan County Senior High School and St. Claire Healthcare, which the city says employs 1,200. Lewis, Carter, Elliott, Morgan, Menifee, Bath and Fleming counties adjoin it, and part of the Daniel Boone National Forest falls inside the line.

The county's early story shapes today's map. Surveyors from Pennsylvania are believed to have explored the area in 1773, and the first settlement grew at Farmers, about ten miles west of Morehead. Clearfield came second and had the first sawmill in the county. Morehead, third in line, was founded in 1854 by a colonel who bought the land and named the town for a governor. A tax levied on Morehead in 1896 paid for hard-surfaced roads, and that road system reached Farmers by 1920.

Census QuickFacts gives the housing picture:

  • July 2025 population estimate of 24,476, which is 0.7 percent under 2020.
  • Owners occupy 61.5 percent of homes, across 9,592 households averaging 2.25 people.
  • Typical home value $161,800; typical gross rent $825.
  • Midpoint household income $54,321, with 25.9 percent of adults holding a bachelor's degree.
  • Eight building permits in 2025, and broadband in 93.4 percent of households.

The 2020 census measured a median age of 32.7, and new construction is thin, so most listings are existing houses.

faqs.q: What is the last day for the Rowan County discount?
faqs.a: The county lists a 2 percent discount for bills paid before November 30. The printed amount is then due through December 31, and 5 percent is added in January.

faqs.q: Does the Rowan County sheriff take credit cards?
faqs.a: Yes: Visa, MasterCard, American Express and Discover, through a vendor that charges 2.49 percent above $60 or $1.50 below it. Cash, checks and money orders are welcome too.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Rowan County sheriff's tax office?
faqs.a: Call (606) 784-5446 or visit 600 West Main Street in Morehead, weekdays 8 AM to 4 PM.

faqs.q: Is a payment plan possible once a Rowan County bill is delinquent?
faqs.a: Yes, through the County Attorney's office: 10 percent of the bill is due on signing day and the remainder is split into monthly payments. Sign before the sale to keep investors out.

faqs.q: Who handles questions about a Rowan County valuation?
faqs.a: The Property Valuation Administrator, at (606) 784-5512. A conference there comes before any appeal at the County Clerk.
